Delete the function body so getPrice reverts silently (returns nothing), which changes the return value from an empty int256 (0) to a revert.
Return a non-zero constant int256 (e.g., 42) instead of the default zero value.

Remove the view modifier so the function can be called only internally/transactionally, but more importantly make it not view, potentially allowing state changes in future overrides—here the immediate behavioral change is that it ceases to be a read-only function, altering the call semantics.
Delete the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier from requestPrice, allowing anyone to call it and change the observed event emission behavior.
Replace the modifier body with an empty block, making it always pass and allowing anyone to call requestPrice.
Replace the require statement in the modifier with a condition that always fails (require(false)), causing requestPrice to always revert.
Move the emit statement before the modifier, by inlining the modifier body and placing emit first, changing behavior when caller is not the optimistic asserter (event emitted before revert).
Remove the entire body of assertionResolvedCallback so the function does nothing, changing its behavior from a no-op revert (due to onlyOptimisticAsserter) to a no-op that succeeds for any caller.
Remove the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier from assertionResolvedCallback, making it callable by anyone instead of only the optimistic asserter.
Change assertionResolvedCallback to always revert regardless of caller.
